description: One run per deal, as many at once as you have in the pipe. Notes, links and answers stay on that deal's run; what you change about the process, kept, is how the next deal starts.
name: Due diligence on a deal

steps.description: What has to be true for this to be a good deal. Every step below is a test of it.
steps.title: Write the thesis in one sentence

steps.description: Today, in one message: incorporation papers, cap table, financials, material contracts, IP assignments. A list sent in pieces is a data room that arrives in pieces.
steps.title: Send the request list

steps.description: Every SAFE, note and option grant on the cap table, and the cap table matching the documents.
steps.title: Who owns what

steps.description: Every founder and contractor has assigned their work to the company, including what they wrote before it existed.
steps.title: Who owns the code

steps.description: Revenue in the model against money that arrived. A gap is a question, not yet a problem.
steps.title: The numbers against the bank

steps.description: End to end, before the next call. What it does on your phone outranks what the deck says it does.
steps.title: Use the product yourself

steps.description: Ask what they would use if it disappeared tomorrow.
steps.title: Call two customers they did not pick

steps.description: Somebody who worked with them, not somebody they gave you.
steps.title: One reference on each founder

steps.description: Litigation, regulation, privacy, a dependency on one platform. Write it down even when the answer is none.
steps.title: Anything that would stop the round

steps.description: A flag with nothing that would clear it is a pass dressed up as a question.
steps.title: List the red flags and what would clear each

steps.description: Invest, pass, or one more question with a date on it. Written, with the reason.
steps.title: Decide

steps.description: A step that was missing, one that was a waste of time. Keep it, and the next deal runs the better version.
steps.title: What this deal taught the process
